entries.topic: Egri Bikavér: at least four varieties, not three
entries.claim: The Eger record (summary, made.winemaking, law.classification, law.tiers Classicus, exam[0], cards[0].b) and the Hungary country record (exam[1], question r-1ozia0r0) say Egri Bikavér is a blend of at least three varieties, and the country question says the same of Szekszárdi Bikavér.
entries.finding: The Egri Bikavér product specification that applies to wines marketed from the 2023/2024 wine year asks for at least four varieties, each above 5 per cent of the blend, with Kékfrankos at 30 to 65 per cent and the largest share; the earlier Eger texts asked for more, not fewer (five varieties in the upper tiers of the text applicable from 2012, struck to four in a later draft), and three is the count of older rules (a Szekszárd text of 2009 still wrote three), not of either specification in force. The Szekszárd specification, fourth version, applicable from 15 March 2024, also asks for at least four varieties, with Kékfrankos at 45 per cent or more and Kadarka at 5 per cent or more. The national wine body's own pages and the 2024 Hungarian Wine Summit material give the same: four grapes, Kékfrankos 30 to 65 per cent at Eger. The oak minimums the record gives (six months for Classicus, twelve for Superior and Grand Superior) hold.

entries.why: Three is the count of a superseded rule: both Bikavér specifications in force ask for four, so every line that teaches three is wrong for the exam and for a guest.

refuter.note: Tried to refute with the tier rows of the Egri Bikavér specification for the 2023/2024 wine year (search summaries drawn from the ministry registers): Classicus asks at least four varieties, each above 5 per cent, Kékfrankos 30 to 65 per cent and the largest share, eight days on the skins and six months in wood; Superior gives the same Kékfrankos band, with Turán and Bíborkadarka held to 10 per cent between them; Grand Superior again asks four varieties above 5 per cent. Secondary pages that give five varieties or a 50 per cent ceiling for the upper tiers repeat the text applicable from 2012. The second version of the Eger specification is where three varieties and no variety above half come from; versions 3 and 4 (the latter for grapes harvested after 1 August 2017) already ask four. One wrinkle: versions 3 and 4 let an organic Classicus be blended from three varieties; the summaries of the 2023/2024 text show no such clause, so four is the rule and the organic allowance is noted as unsettled. Szekszárd: version 4, for wine released from 15 March 2024, asks four varieties, Kékfrankos at 45 per cent or more and Kadarka at 5 per cent or more; version 1 had asked three and 35 per cent, so the country question's three was out of date for both towns. All eight olds occur once in hungary.1.json at the paths named, and each new line reads in place; the Classicus tier, exam line and card stay true of every tier. Completeness: the Szekszárd record (hungary.2.json), the Régionale primer (four, Kékfrankos the largest share), the Certified primer (largest share) and the Advanced answer (four, handled in L3-02) already agree; no other line in js/, the region fragments, the CMS questions, rewrite/categories or the grape fragments gives three (blaufrankisch.json carries the count only in its review notes).

entries.topic: Tokaj: dry single vineyard Furmint from about the turn of the century
entries.claim: The Hungary country record (overview, grapes[0].styles) and the Tokaj record (summary, exam[5]) date dry Furmint from single vineyards, and its class, to the 1990s: in the same decade as the rebuilt estates, since the 1990s, the dry Furmint movement of the 1990s.
entries.finding: Dry Tokaji was made in the 1990s: the first commercial dry wines of the post communist years came from the new estates in the early 1990s, and dry Furmint had long been made as the base wine for Aszú. The single vineyard dry Furmint that changed Tokaj's view of the style dates from the 2000 vintage, an Úrágya wine made at Mád after a year of poor botrytis. So the 1990s is right for dry Tokaji and wrong for single vineyard dry Furmint of class; about the turn of the century is true of both. The Szent Tamás note (the 2000s) already agrees and stays.

entries.topic: Tokaji Aszú at the table: 10 to 12 degrees, warmer than the sweet whites row
entries.claim: The Tokaj record serves Aszú at 10 to 12 degrees Celsius (wines[0].note, exam[6]); the service reference serves sweet whites with Tokaji named at 6 to 8 C (the temperatures row) and Tokaji Aszú with Sauternes at 6 to 8 C (the digestifs row); the Furmint grape page says sweet Aszú colder, as for Sauternes.
entries.finding: No statement of the Tokaj wine community was found. The Tokaj houses put Aszú at 10 to 12 degrees Celsius (a Mád house's Aszú sheets), 10 to 13 (a Tokaj estate's six puttonyos sheet) and 12 to 14 (an Aszú on the national wine body's fair pages); the national body's Furmint page puts late harvest Furmint at 8 to 10. The serving references put Tokaji colder than its makers but not as cold as 6 to 8: the Swedish monopoly serves Sauternes and Tokaji at 8 to 10, and a serving guide gives Tokaji Aszú 7 to 12. So the record's 10 to 12 is Tokaj's own figure and stands, the 6 to 8 of the two service rows is colder than any source read for Tokaji, and the Furmint page follows the rows. The sweet whites band itself (Sauternes, ice wine, late harvest) is not in question here and stays at 6 to 8.

entries.topic: Furmint: botrytis prone, skin thickness dropped
entries.claim: The Régionale row for Furmint (INTRO_GRAPES) ends Thin-skinned and botrytis-prone; the Tokaj record calls Furmint thin skinned and botrytis prone (grapes[0].styles); the Régionale question i-2zibe7e9 gives thin skins as a clue to Furmint.
entries.finding: Every source read agrees that Furmint is prone to botrytis, with a loose bunch and late ripening that let the rot in; on the skin they split. A government vine sheet and an importer's glossary call the skin thin and tie the rot to it; two wine references call the skin thick, one of them tying the rot to the thick skin, and no Hungarian variety description was found to settle it. The Furmint grape page already leaves the skin out for this reason. So the skin claim goes and botrytis prone stays.

The stem of i-2zibe7e9 still keys Furmint alone (Hárslevelű also rots nobly but is not the mainstay and carries less acid), its options and explanation stay true, and the text stays ASCII; the stem change moves the minted id, so the integrator pins i-2zibe7e9 (it is named by id in .scripts/cms/map/hungary.json and the CMS review notes, and check-ids.py needs it logged). entries.topic: Tannat and Petit Verdot rows: the climate and the acid dials
entries.claim: The Régionale rows (INTRO_GRAPES) give Tannat climate Warm and acid 3, and Petit Verdot acid 2; TASTE gives Tannat a moderate climate and acid medium plus, and the profiles give Tannat medium to high acid and Petit Verdot medium plus.
entries.finding: The acid dial runs 1 to 3, and the rows read TASTE's medium plus as 3 for most reds (Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc, Blaufränkisch, Aglianico, Mencía and Tannat) and as 2 for a few (Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel, Touriga Nacional), so medium plus sits on either side of the line; the sources read put Tannat's acidity at moderately high to high (and one chart at medium) and the profile says medium to high, so Tannat's 3 holds, and Petit Verdot's 2 is a defensible reading of medium plus that no source or profile shows wrong. The climate is another matter: every other grape TASTE calls moderate reads Moderate, Cool to moderate, Moderate to warm or wider in the rows, never Warm alone; Tannat's homes are Madiran under the Atlantic's rain and mild, damp autumns and Uruguay's humid, maritime Canelones, which the Codex's own records describe so, and the grape page's ladder sets them moderate with only Cafayate and Paso Robles warm. So the climate moves to Moderate to warm and both acid dials stay.

refuter.note: Tested the dials against the shipped data: TASTE (not touched) gives Tannat acid 2 and clim moderate, and its acid 2 (medium plus) reads as 3 in the Régionale rows for Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc, Blaufränkisch, Aglianico, Mencía and Tannat and as 2 for Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel and Touriga Nacional, so neither acid dial is shown wrong. The climate is: the grape page (tannat.json) puts Madiran, Irouléguy, Canelones and Maldonado on the moderate rung and only Cafayate, northern Uruguay and Paso Robles on the warm one, and Uruguay's humid, maritime climate and Madiran's Atlantic autumns are moderate. Moderate to warm is a value nine rows already use (Merlot among them) and codex53 only prints it, so nothing parses it. The old occurs once in INTRO_GRAPES. The same row's trap, one of the most tannic grapes, is hedged in the form L2-06 accepted for Sagrantino and stays.

entries.topic: Zweigelt row: Austria's most planted red (report only)
entries.claim: The Régionale row for Zweigelt (INTRO_GRAPES) gives reg Austria, starred, (most-planted red) and the trap Austria's most-planted red: a Blaufränkisch × St. Laurent cross; juicy and approachable.
entries.finding: The rank holds today: the Austrian figures put Zweigelt at about 13.4 per cent of the vineyard in 2023/2024, some 6,130 hectares, ahead of Blaufränkisch at 5.8 per cent, with all red grapes about 30 per cent; it is the most planted red by a wide margin. The hyphen in most-planted is a compound modifier, not a dash.

entries.topic: Viognier and Gewürztraminer: ginger is Gewürztraminer's
entries.claim: The Viognier profile in js/reference.js lists Honeysuckle, violet, jasmine, musk and ginger among its other notes, while the Gewürztraminer profile's confuse line says Viognier is apricot and honeysuckle without the lychee or spice, and the Codex's grape table makes ginger Gewürztraminer's lead note.
entries.finding: The references read give Viognier apricot, peach, tangerine, honeysuckle, violet and rose, with musk; a grape guide's primary list (tangerine, peach, mango, honeysuckle, rose) and a merchant's guide have no ginger. Ginger does turn up in Viognier, but as a secondary hint: one guide lists it among the layers, and several Condrieu tasting notes give it (spiced ginger on a merchant's page for one Condrieu, a whisper of ginger spice on another, ginger in drinkers' notes on a third). Ginger, with clove and allspice, is what the Codex and the guides give Gewürztraminer as a lead note, and the Gewürztraminer profile's confuse line and the grape table both teach Viognier without that spice. Cutting the two words from the Viognier profile makes the records agree, and the confuse line stays as it is.

targets.new: other:"Honeysuckle, violet, jasmine and musk;

sources.says: Apricot, white peach and honeysuckle, layered with orange blossom, jasmine, ginger and a hint of musk: the one guide read that names ginger, among the layers.

entries.why: Two Codex records pulled apart on one note; the sources make ginger Gewürztraminer's and at most a passing hint in Viognier, so two words leave the Viognier profile and nothing else moves.

refuter.note: The finding understated ginger in Viognier: a search of Condrieu notes found it on several, as a secondary hint, so ginger is not false of the grape, and the finding now says so. The cut still stands, for the reason the second sommeliers gave: a profile's other notes are what a blind taster steers by, and ginger is the lead note the Codex teaches for Gewürztraminer; the Gewürztraminer confuse line and the grape table (whose Gewürztraminer entry says Viognier has no lychee or ginger) already teach Viognier without it, so one record pulled against two. Softening the confuse line instead would leave the grape table disagreeing. The old occurs once in GRAPES (js/reference.js, hand held), and the line keeps four notes and its rhythm. Completeness: no other Viognier line in js/reference.js, js/data-grapes-plus.js, INTRO_GRAPES, the CMS or the banks names ginger.

entries.topic: Superlatives of judgement: Naoussa's producers and Touriga Nacional
entries.claim: The Naoussa record calls the oldest house's Grande Reserve the classic old-school Naoussa on any list (producers[0].why) and another estate's old vine wine the top old-vine bottling (producers[2].why), and calls a third house's Ramnista the modern reference for structured Naoussa (producers[1].why); the Régionale row for Touriga Nacional (INTRO_GRAPES) opens its trap on Portugal's top red.
entries.finding: Each is a ranking of the Codex's own, which the house rules keep out of the Codex. The facts beside them stand and are kept: the house founded at Naoussa in 1879 and its long aged Grande Reserve in the old style (the record's own wines and places notes describe that style), the estate's old vine bottling, and Touriga Nacional's deep colour, floral lift and firm structure and its place among the Port grapes. Nobody living is named in the new words; the 1879 founder named in the first line is long dead.

targets.new: and whose Grande Reserve shows the long-aged, old-school style of Naoussa.

targets.old: and whose Earth and Sky is the top old-vine bottling.
targets.new: and whose Earth and Sky is its old-vine bottling.

targets.new: Ramnista is a structured Naoussa in the modern style

targets.old: Portugal’s top red: deep colour, floral lift, firm structure.
targets.new: Portugal’s signature red: deep colour, floral lift, firm structure.

entries.why: The house rule: no superlative of judgement (top, classic on any list); the lines keep their facts and lose the ranking, and the grape row reads signature as the other rows do (Rueda, South Africa, Uruguay).

refuter.note: The three original olds occur once each and read well in place; the founder of 1879 is long dead and the house of 1997 is named by its house, not its founder. Completeness within the record: the producers list carried a third ranking the entry left, Ramnista as the modern reference for structured Naoussa, a benchmark claim of the same kind as the classic on any list; it is added as a target (the old occurs once) and keeps its fact, a structured Naoussa in the modern style. The record's other words (the classic style of the old houses, much classic Grande Reserve, the reference appellation for Xinomavro) describe a style or the appellation's standing, not a ranking of a producer, and stay. Touriga Nacional: no other line ranks it Portugal's top red (the Douro question's most prized and the Régionale stem generally rated the finest for Port report a reputation and stay). Not added, since no second sommelier flagged them: Dão's Encruzado is Portugal's noblest white and the other judgement words across the L3 records (see unsettled).

entries.topic: Source titles that name the living authors of Wine Grapes
entries.claim: Thirty four source titles in the region fragments cite Wine Grapes with its three living authors named in the title (Wine Grapes, Robinson, Harding and Vouillamoz, entry on ...; Wine Grapes (Robinson, Harding, Vouillamoz); Wine Grapes (Robinson, Harding and Vouillamoz): ...).
entries.finding: The codex56 articles cite the book as Wine Grapes (Penguin, 2012), and other records already write Wine Grapes, entries on ...; each title below takes that form and keeps its own entries (for example Wine Grapes (Penguin, 2012), entry on Xinomavro). Where the same title stands more than once in a file, the old runs back to the source before it so that each old occurs once. The hand files (js/data-service-ref.js, js/reference.js, js/data-grapes-plus.js, js/data-intro.js, the primers, the Advanced and Master banks, the grape fragments and the CMS subjects) name none of the three in a shown source; js/regions/*.json carry the same titles and follow from the fragments by the build.

entries.topic: Burgenland: Zweigelt leads the Seewinkel, not the whole state
entries.claim: The Burgenland record calls Zweigelt the most planted grape of the Seewinkel and of Burgenland as a whole (grapes[1].styles) and says so again in a trap (traps[6]).
entries.finding: Austrian Wine's figures put Blaufränkisch first in Burgenland and Zweigelt a close second: 2,437 ha against 2,337 ha in its documentation of 2021, and 2,394 ha (21 per cent) against 2,239 ha (19 per cent) on its current Burgenland page; the census of 2020 also gives Blaufränkisch, 2,534 ha, as Burgenland's leading red. In the Neusiedlersee area, the lake's east and north shores, Zweigelt is first, about 1,398 ha or 23 per cent. Austria-wide Zweigelt still leads the reds (L3-07).

targets.new: The most planted grape of the Seewinkel:

targets.new: Zweigelt is the most planted grape of the Seewinkel, not of Burgenland as a whole, where Blaufränkisch is narrowly ahead; Blaufränkisch also leads Mittelburgenland and the south.

sources.says: Blaufränkisch, 2,437 ha, is first in Burgenland, closely followed by Zweigelt, 2,337 ha; Zweigelt leads Niederösterreich.

entries.why: The g8 note named the Burgenland record beside the Régionale row; the national body's figures put Blaufränkisch narrowly first there, so the state wide rank goes, the Seewinkel rank (true) stays, and the trap turns on the real confusion.

refuter.note: Added by the second reader under L3-07's completeness. Both olds occur once in austria.json at the paths named; check-fragment passes on austria.json with both edits applied in a scratch copy. The Seewinkel claim rests on the Neusiedlersee figures (the Seewinkel is the larger part of that area). No figure is written into the Codex, so the trap stays true while the two grapes stay close; if a later census reverses them, only the clause narrowly ahead moves. No other line in js/, the fragments, the CMS, rewrite/categories or the grape fragments ranks Zweigelt in Burgenland.

entries.topic: Douro and Greek planting ranks (report only)
entries.claim: The Douro record and the Portugal country record call Touriga Franca the most planted grape of the Douro (grapes, exam, trap, card and question r-ksi8jaas); the Greece country record and the Nemea record call Agiorgitiko Greece's most planted red and Nemea Greece's largest red appellation (summary, grapes, law, exam, cards and questions).
entries.finding: Each rank holds. The Douro's own institute gives Touriga Franca 10,727 ha in 2023, 25 per cent of 42,980 ha, ahead of Tinta Roriz (14.3 per cent) and Touriga Nacional (10.3 per cent). The Greek national wine body gives Agiorgitiko as the most planted red variety and third overall, and calls Nemea Greece's largest PDO zone for red wine.

sources.says: Touriga Franca 10,727 ha, 25 per cent of 42,980 ha (2023); Tinta Roriz 6,163 ha; Touriga Nacional 4,432 ha.

entries.why: The g12 note named these ranks as volatile; each is true on the governing body's current figures, so, as with Zweigelt in Austria, nothing changes.

refuter.note: Added by the second reader: the g12 note named the Douro and Nemea ranks and no entry tested them. Each holds on a primary body's figures. One fact turned up in passing and is left for the owner, since no second sommelier flagged it: the Nemea zone takes in two villages of Argolida (Gymno and Malandreni) beside fifteen of Corinthia, while the record's law.classification says villages in the Corinthia regional unit and its first tier the delimited villages of Corinthia (see unsettled).
